newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World sees China land bank adequate.
newsitem.headline: New World sees China land bank adequate.

text.p: A top manager of New World Development Co Ltd said on Thursday the company had a sufficient land bank in China for future development projects and spinoffs of its property business.

"We currently have sufficient land bank (in China) for our development plans in the next 10 to 20 years and we will also aggressively expand our property investment if opportunities arise," managing director Henry Cheng said at a news conference.
"We have issued convertible bonds preparing for the future spinoff of (our) China property business," Cheng said.
"And the land bank is big enough for the spinoff."

Its unit New World China Finance Ltd in October launched a US$350 million issue of mandatorily convertible bonds, which would be convertible into shares of New World China Ltd in the event of an initial public offering in end-1999.

Cheng said spinoffs of the company's property business in China would be in three areas: urban redevelopment, residential and commercial development projects for sale and rental, and land development projects.

With demand for residential properties in China seen rising due to encouragement from Beijing on home-ownership, the company also expects an increase in profits as it would be putting more projects on sale in the next two years, he said.
Cheng also said New World Development was looking into spinning off its construction and civil engineering unit Hip Hing Construction Co Ltd.
But he dismissed speculation that the company planned to spinoff all its subsidiaries.
"It is not our intention to spinoff all the subsidiaries and make New World a holding company," he said.
"New World itself has a lot of activities, all these spinoff exercises represent only about 30 percent...of the total New World capitalisation or portfolio," Cheng added.
The main reason for spinoffs was to allow units to stand on their own, like the company's projects in China, so the parent company could concentrate on development in Hong Kong, he said.
